title: Cache telemetry v2 — metric/tag mapping sheet (old → v2)
body:
Last updated: 2025-02-18 (Logan)

Purpose
- Provide a single mapping between legacy prefix/KV cache metrics/tags and the v2 telemetry spec.
- Clarify: which tags are allowed on metrics, which are hashed/bucketed, and which are only allowed on sampled events.
- Intended users: runtime instrumentation (Omar/Samir), gateway attribution (Ethan/Amara), telemetry pipeline (Nadia/Caleb), dashboards (Sergio/Mei).

Notes / guardrails (read me first)
- v2 splits telemetry into:
  (A) Metrics (high volume): strict tag allowlist + bucketing rules.
  (B) Sampled events (low volume): richer context (tenant_id, request_id, trace_id, prompt_prefix_hash, etc.).
- Do NOT attach request_id, trace_id, prompt hash, raw route name, or raw tenant_id to high-volume metrics.
- Region is required on all v2 metrics.
- For “route” breakdown in metrics, we use route_bucket (hashed) + optional route_group (low-card category) when available.
- For “tenant” breakdown in metrics, we use tenant_bucket (hashed) + tenant_tier. Raw tenant_id is event-only.

Hashing/bucketing conventions (v2)
- route_bucket: uint16, computed as (xxhash64(route_id) % 256). Stored as string ("0".."255").
- tenant_bucket: uint16, computed as (xxhash64(tenant_id) % 512). Stored as string ("0".."511").
- prefix_bucket (event-only): uint16 (xxhash64(normalized_prefix) % 1024) — only emitted on sampled cache_event.
- Hash salt: stable per environment (prod/stage differ). Salt lives in telemetry config; never in code.

====================
TAB 1 — Metric name mapping (legacy → v2)
(Columns) Legacy metric | Legacy meaning | v2 metric | v2 type/unit | Required v2 tags | Notes / transform

1) prefix_cache.hit_total | count of full prefix hits | redwood.cache.kv.lookup.count | counter (count) | region, deployment_mode, cache_outcome, model_family, runtime_build | Use cache_outcome=hit; legacy counted some partial hits as hit (see known issue). Backfill dashboards should treat pre-v2 as “approx”.
2) prefix_cache.miss_total | count of cache misses | redwood.cache.kv.lookup.count | counter (count) | region, deployment_mode, cache_outcome, model_family, runtime_build | Use cache_outcome=miss.
3) prefix_cache.partial_total | partial hit (some tokens reused) | redwood.cache.kv.lookup.count | counter (count) | region, deployment_mode, cache_outcome, model_family, runtime_build | Use cache_outcome=partial.
4) kv_cache.lookup_ms | lookup time | redwood.cache.kv.lookup.latency_ms | histogram (ms) | region, deployment_mode, model_family, runtime_build | No outcome tag (kept off to reduce dimensionality); lookup latency should include negative lookups.
5) kv_cache.insert_total | inserts into cache | redwood.cache.kv.insert.count | counter (count) | region, deployment_mode, model_family, runtime_build | Insert occurs when prefill completes and policy allows.
6) kv_cache.insert_bytes | bytes inserted | redwood.cache.kv.insert.bytes | counter (bytes) | region, deployment_mode, model_family, runtime_build | Bytes = size of KV blocks written.
7) kv_cache.evict_total | evictions | redwood.cache.kv.evict.count | counter (count) | region, deployment_mode, model_family, evict_reason, runtime_build | evict_reason is low-card enum (pressure|ttl|policy|manual).
8) kv_cache.resident_bytes | cache size | redwood.cache.kv.resident.bytes | gauge (bytes) | region, deployment_mode, model_family, runtime_build | Emitted per host; pipeline aggregates to fleet-level.
9) cache.hit_rate | legacy computed ratio | (removed) | n/a | n/a | Do not emit ratios as metrics; dashboards compute hit_rate = hit / (hit+miss+partial).
10) prefill.latency_ms | end-to-end prefill | redwood.infer.prefill.latency_ms | histogram (ms) | region, deployment_mode, model_family, runtime_build | Not cache-specific; used for saved_prefill_ms validation.
11) cache.saved_prefill_ms_est | estimated ms saved | redwood.cache.kv.saved_prefill_ms | counter (ms) | region, deployment_mode, cache_outcome, model_family, runtime_build | Only emit on hit/partial; miss emits 0 (omit rather than 0).
12) cache.hit_bytes | bytes reused from cache | redwood.cache.kv.hit.bytes | counter (bytes) | region, deployment_mode, cache_outcome, model_family, runtime_build | On partial: only count reused bytes, not newly computed.
13) gateway.cacheable_prompt_total | “cacheable prompt” denom | redwood.cache.kv.cacheable_prompt.count | counter (count) | region, deployment_mode, model_family, runtime_build | Cacheable prompt = passes normalization + policy allows caching.
14) gateway.prompt_total | total prompts | redwood.infer.request.count | counter (count) | region, deployment_mode, request_kind, model_family | request_kind=chat|completion|embeddings (cache only relevant for generation).
15) cache.policy_mismatch_total | policy mismatch events | redwood.cache.kv.policy_mismatch.count | counter (count) | region, deployment_mode, mismatch_reason, model_family, runtime_build | mismatch_reason low-card (disabled|ttl_too_low|max_seq|model_incompatible|routing_fragment).

====================
TAB 2 — Tag mapping (legacy → v2) w/ allowlist + treatment
(Columns) Legacy tag | Example | v2 tag | Allowed on metrics? | Treatment | Notes

A) Tenant/customer attribution
- customer | "acme-co" | tenant_id | NO (events only) | event-only | Raw tenant identifiers prohibited on metrics.
- account_id | "11872" | tenant_id | NO (events only) | event-only | Same as above.
- plan | "enterprise" | tenant_tier | YES | pass-through (enum) | Allowed values: free|pro|enterprise|internal.
- (none) | n/a | tenant_bucket | YES | hashed bucket | tenant_bucket = xxhash64(tenant_id) % 512 computed at gateway/control-plane.

B) Route / endpoint attribution
- endpoint | "/v1/chat/completions" | route_group | YES | normalized | route_group is low-card coarse grouping: chat_completions|completions|responses|internal_batch.
- route_name | "support-bot-prod" | route_id | NO (events only) | event-only | Raw route_id ok only on sampled events.
- (none) | n/a | route_bucket | YES | hashed bucket | route_bucket = xxhash64(route_id) % 256.
- deployment | "dedicated-acme" | deployment_id | NO (events only) | event-only | Too high cardinality.

C) Model attribution
- model | "llama-70b-instruct" | model_family | YES | normalized | model_family collapses variants: e.g., llama3_70b, qwen2_72b.
- model_version | "2025-02-01" | model_version | NO (events only) | event-only | Too high churn for metrics; dashboards can join via events when debugging.
- engine | "redwood-runtime" | runtime_build | YES | normalized | runtime_build is low-ish cardinality (runtime train build id). Keep string short.

D) Location / deployment mode
- cluster | "us-east-1-prod" | region | YES | normalized | region values: us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1, etc.
- dc | "iad" | region | YES | mapped | Mapped to region where possible; else set region=unknown and emit mapping warning once/hour.
- mode | "hosted" | deployment_mode | YES | enum | hosted|dedicated|private.
- vpc_id | "vpc-123" | (none) | NO | drop | High-card + sensitive.

E) Runtime host/process detail (generally NOT allowed)
- pod | "runtime-7f9c..." | (none) | NO | drop | Use runtime_build + region. Host-level debug via logs, not metrics tags.
- host | "ip-10-..." | (none) | NO | drop | Same.
- gpu | "a100-80g" | gpu_sku | NO (metrics) / YES (events) | event-only (for now) | Decision: keep gpu_sku off metrics until cardinality budget re-eval; can be derived in perf datasets.
- shard | "12" | (none) | NO | drop | Not stable.

F) Cache context
- cache | "prefix" | cache_kind | YES | enum | cache_kind=kv_prefix (reserved for future multi-cache).
- cache_namespace | "tenant" | cache_namespace | YES | enum | tenant|shared|internal.
- cache_policy | "ttl=300" | cache_policy | NO (metrics) / YES (events) | event-only | Too many distinct strings; use policy_id event-only.
- ttl_s | "300" | cache_ttl_s_bucket | YES | bucketed | Buckets: 0, 60, 300, 900, 3600, 14400, 86400, other.

G) Outcome classification
- hit | "true" | cache_outcome | YES | enum | hit|miss|partial. (No booleans.)
- miss_reason | "not_found" | miss_reason | NO (metrics) / YES (events) | event-only | Keep detailed reasons out of metrics.

====================
TAB 3 — Aggregation / pipeline rules (what gets dropped or rewritten)
- If any metric arrives with disallowed tags, pipeline will:
  1) Drop the disallowed tag(s)
  2) Increment redwood.telemetry.dropped_tag.count (internal)
  3) If the metric still violates allowlist (e.g., unknown tag), drop metric sample and increment redwood.telemetry.dropped_metric.count
- v2 metrics must include: region, deployment_mode, model_family, runtime_build (except request.count which omits runtime_build).
- cache_outcome is allowed ONLY on lookup.count, hit.bytes, saved_prefill_ms. Do not attach cache_outcome to every metric.

====================
TAB 4 — Dashboard query compatibility notes (so we don’t break Console)
- Hit rate:
  hit_rate = sum(lookup.count{cache_outcome=hit}) / sum(lookup.count{cache_outcome in [hit,miss,partial]})
- Cacheable prompt ratio:
  cacheable_ratio = sum(cacheable_prompt.count) / sum(infer.request.count{request_kind in [chat,completion]})
- Saved prefill (ms):
  saved_prefill_ms_per_req = sum(saved_prefill_ms) / sum(infer.request.count{request_kind in [chat,completion]})
- Route drilldown:
  Use route_bucket for “top N buckets”; for human readable route names we require sampled events join (Console debug panel only).

====================
Open questions / TODOs
- Confirm whether model_family mapping table lives in gateway (control plane) vs runtime.
- Decide if gpu_sku can be added to metrics for Dedicated only (bounded SKU set) without breaking global budget.
- Confirm tenant_bucket modulus (512) aligns with pipeline storage constraints (Mei/Caleb to validate).
- Determine whether to introduce route_group for Private deployments (may not have route_id).

Change log (manual)
- 2025-02-11: Added tenant_bucket/route_bucket definitions; removed model_version from metrics allowlist.
- 2025-02-14: Added cache_ttl_s_bucket and evict_reason tagging.
- 2025-02-18: Clarified policy_mismatch metric; marked gpu_sku as event-only pending ADR follow-up.
